codeReview.summary: The feature correctly updates repo-facing Zig baseline metadata and substantially improves CLI argument parsing, help text, and invalid-usage tests, but the new top-level error handling introduces a runtime regression: it now exits successfully for every `error.WriteFailed`, not just true broken-pipe cases.

issues.description: `main` now converts any `error.WriteFailed` into exit code 0. That is broader than the intended closed-pipe behavior: `OutputWriter.flush` in `src/parser/evtx/output.zig:105` maps every flush failure to `error.WriteFailed`, so a non-pipe stdout failure can now be silently reported as success instead of surfacing an error.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared runtime guidance does not currently call out that `error.WriteFailed` is a generic writer/flush failure in this codebase, not a broken-pipe-specific signal. Entry points need to distinguish actual pipe closure before treating that error as success.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `src/parser/evtx/output.zig:105` returns `error.WriteFailed` for any `typed.flush()` failure, while `src/main.zig:61` now treats every `error.WriteFailed` as a clean exit.

summary: Reviewed the transcript skeleton, handoff, and commit `fa867dae8d64ea04aae2f2231f3c8e0bc32ca298` for `declare-zig-0-16-baseline-and-build-path`. The feature is close, but scrutiny fails because `src/main.zig` now suppresses all `error.WriteFailed` failures as successful exits, which overreaches the intended closed-pipe handling and masks real stdout write/flush errors.
